title: Embeddings workload: high-QPS small-payload generator + throughput and tail latency reporting
creator: Rina Kobayashi
body:
Context
- We need a representative embeddings workload in the Q1 2026 perf suite that mirrors production traffic: high QPS, small inputs, latency-sensitive, and strongly impacted by batching/queueing under load.
- Unlike chat, the primary KPI is not TTFT/TPOT; it’s throughput (req/s) with strict tail latency (p95/p99) under steady concurrency.

Goal
Implement an embeddings workload generator + harness mode that:
1) Produces stable throughput numbers (req/s) and tail latency (p50/p95/p99) for embeddings endpoints.
2) Captures enough attribution to debug deltas (scheduler queue time, batch sizes, GPU utilization signals where available).
3) Is fully reproducible and wired into the canonical run-manifest/results schema (ADR-0172).

Non-goals (this ticket)
- Not onboarding new embedding models beyond what the suite already targets for Q1 (we will use the curated catalog entry for embeddings; model selection and region/SKU matrix tracked in the baseline plan).
- Not adding customer-facing benchmark marketing content.

Workload definition (v1)
Workload name
- embeddings_high_qps_v1

Request shape
- Endpoint: /v1/embeddings (or Redwood SDK equivalent)
- Input: small payloads, single-input per request (no giant batched client payloads).
- Token length distribution (server-side tokenized length; derived from telemetry bins, no prompt content stored):
  - 60%: 8–32 tokens
  - 30%: 33–128 tokens
  - 10%: 129–256 tokens
- Output: fixed-size embedding vector (model-specific dimension), no streaming.

Traffic shape
- Steady-state sustained load with controlled concurrency (not pure open-loop firehose).
- Test phases:
  1) Warmup: 90s (discard metrics)
  2) Ramp: 60s (linearly increase concurrency to target)
  3) Measure: 5m steady state (collect metrics)
  4) Cooldown: 30s (optional; used only to flush logs/artifacts)
- Concurrency targets:
  - Default: 256 in-flight requests per host (configurable)
  - Sweep mode: [64, 128, 256, 512] (used in baseline sweeps when capacity allows)

Batching/caching assumptions
- No prefix/KV caching (not applicable).
- Server-side continuous batching is allowed and expected (we’re measuring “realistic serving” not a single-request microbenchmark).
- Report both “scheduler on” (default) and “batching disabled” only when explicitly requested for investigations; default suite run keeps production-like scheduler settings.

Measurement boundaries
- Latency definition: client-observed end-to-end latency from request send (after connection established) to response received, plus server-side breakdown tags where available.
- For noise control, the harness uses persistent HTTP connections and avoids per-request TLS handshakes.
- Results export includes both:
  - e2e latency percentiles (primary)
  - server timing subcomponents (best-effort): queue_wait_ms, batch_assembly_ms (if runtime emits), and model_exec_ms (if available)

Required metrics (results schema)
Throughput
- req_per_s (overall)
- success_req_per_s
- error_rate (4xx/5xx split)

Latency (ms)
- latency_ms_p50 / p95 / p99
- latency_ms_p99_9 (optional, when sample size supports)

Saturation / health indicators
- in_flight (avg/max)
- queue_depth (if available)
- batch_size_p50 / p95 (if available)

Reproducibility fields
- workload seed (fixed default; override allowed)
- request length histogram config (bins and weights)
- concurrency target(s)
- duration per phase
- region / GPU SKU / driver+CUDA / runtime build tag (from run manifest)

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Workload generator implemented (configurable distributions + concurrency controller).
- [x] Harness outputs a single results artifact per run: JSON + CSV summary with percentiles + throughput.
- [x] Output conforms to the canonical schema from ENG-4822 (validated in CI).
- [x] Warmup/ramp/measure phases implemented to reduce variance.
- [x] Documented run command + example manifest checked into repo.
- [x] One baseline dry-run executed on benchmark fleet (A100 and/or H100) and posted to run tracker.

Implementation notes
- We observed in earlier prototypes that the bottleneck can shift to client-side serialization/logging at very high QPS. The harness must:
  - Minimize per-request logging (aggregate counters; sample errors)
  - Use async I/O and fixed-size buffers where possible
  - Pre-generate request payloads for each token-length bin to avoid per-request tokenization work on the driver side
- Ensure the harness uses monotonic clocks and records per-phase timestamps in the run manifest for later comparisons.

Links
- Umbrella: ENG-4821 (Q1 2026 perf baseline kickoff + scope)
- Schema: ENG-4822 (run manifest + results schema)
- GitHub PR (benchmark-lab): PR-21488 "embeddings high-qps mode and throughput report" (merged)

Rollout / follow-ups
- Hook into perf-canary nightly suite after gating thresholds are calibrated (tracked in ENG-4828).
- Add dashboard panels for embeddings (req/s + p99) in baseline dashboards spec (tracked separately under dashboarding workstream).
comments: 2025-11-19 — Rina Kobayashi (creator): Creating as part of the representative suite workstream. Embeddings is currently under-measured; we need a stable high-QPS mode with tail latency percentiles and req/s.

2025-11-26 — Claire Dubois: Please ensure we’re not accidentally measuring client connect/TLS overhead. We should treat this as “steady-state service latency” with persistent connections. Also, encode the length distribution in the manifest (bins+weights), not as freeform text.
2025-12-03 — Sean Gallagher: For benchmark fleet variance, the warmup+ramp separation matters. Also recommend we cap per-request logging; we’ve seen perf tests become driver-bound at high QPS.

2025-12-11 — Marcus Reed (assignee): Drafted workload spec and started implementing embeddings mode in benchmark-lab. Plan: open-loop option for stress testing, but default to closed-loop (fixed concurrency) for stable latency percentiles.

2025-12-19 — Jonas Weber: Confirmed the proposed token-length bins match the telemetry cohort we extracted for embeddings traffic (no prompt content). Please include the ability to re-weight bins per customer cohort later, but v1 can ship with the default mix.
2026-01-08 — Marcus Reed: PR up: benchmark-lab PR-21488. Includes: embeddings mode, warmup/ramp/measure phases, results export with req/s + p50/p95/p99, and manifest validation hook.

2026-01-14 — Logan Wright: Reviewed tagging/metrics export. Request: add explicit fields for total_requests, successful_requests, and error counts so dashboards can compute rates reliably without inference from time series.
2026-01-18 — Marcus Reed: Addressed review feedback: added total/success/error counters, made connections persistent by default, and reduced per-request logging to sampled errors only.

2026-01-23 — Rina Kobayashi: Ran first dry-run on benchmark fleet and attached results to the baseline run tracker (Drive). Numbers look stable across repeated runs once warmup is applied; remaining variance correlates with GPU clock drift (tracked in noise scratchpad).
2026-01-29 — Marcus Reed: Merged PR-21488. Marking ticket Done. Next step is wiring embeddings panels into dashboards and including this workload in perf-canary (ENG-4828).
